rafa loop wait — wait on a session until a reason --until names happens

Usage:
  rafa loop wait [-s|--session-id=<string>] [--until=<string>]
    [--timeout=<string>]

Description:
  Follows a loop run until a reason `--until` asks for happens, then prints one
  `rafa·` line naming it and exits with that reason's code. It reads the run's
  events file, `.rafa/runs/<session-id>.events.ndjson`, from its first line, so
  a run that has already ended still answers, and reads the run's record and
  probes its pid every 5 seconds. The reasons: `pr`, event pr, exits 0; `no-pr`,
  event no-pr, exits 10; `halt`, event halt, exits 11; `error`, event error,
  exits 12; `blocked`, event task-blocked, exits 13; `exit`, the run's pid not
  alive, or its record reading stopped or done, exits 14; `quiet:<minutes>`, no
  event for <minutes> awake minutes, exits 15. `--timeout` reached exits 16, and
  a session it cannot find exits 2. Without `--until` it waits for
  `pr,no-pr,halt,error,exit`; `blocked` and `quiet` are never in that set. Quiet
  minutes and the timeout count time the machine is awake, so a suspended laptop
  never reads as a stuck loop; on macOS the clock keeps counting through sleep,
  so there a long sleep can raise a false `quiet` or an early timeout. A run
  with no events file, from an older rafa, is noted once, and only `exit`,
  `quiet` and the timeout can answer for it. Without `--session-id` it waits on
  the session running on the branch checked out at the project root, or the
  newest one that ran there. With `--output=json` the reason, the event, the
  session's state and the minutes are the data of a `wait` event, and of the
  terminal result when it exits 0.

Flags:
  -s, --session-id   string
      The session to wait on, by the id its record under `.rafa/runs/` is named
      with. Without it, the session running on the branch checked out at the
      project root.
  --until            string
      The reasons to wait for, a comma list of pr, no-pr, halt, error, blocked,
      exit, quiet:<minutes>. `pr,no-pr,halt,error,exit` when it is left out.
  --timeout          string
      How many awake minutes to wait before giving up with exit code 16. No
      limit when it is left out.

Examples:
  rafa loop wait
      Waits on the session of the branch checked out here until it opens a PR,
      ends without one, halts, fails or exits.
  rafa loop wait --session-id=9185b41c-65f7-4dd6-a0c1-6494c4028f0f --until=blocked,exit,quiet:30
      Wakes on a blocked task, the run's end, or 30 awake minutes with no event.
  rafa loop wait --timeout=60 --output=json
      Waits up to an hour awake, then writes the reason, the event and the
      session's state as a wait event.

Outputs:
  text, json

See also:
  rafa loop start, rafa loop stop, rafa loop pause, rafa loop resume, rafa loop
  status, rafa loop list
